headline: Letter supporting zoning change for Carrier's 15 apartments at 222 Main Street and 24 units at 233 Main Street
summary: Town planning staff found that minor zoning changes are needed to allow apartments downtown with no retail space. The zoning application is set for the December meeting, with a Planning Commission referral and a public hearing in January. JHM Group gave an update on the Sessions project at 273 and 296 Riverside Avenue and said historic approval typically takes about a year. Transfers of 30,000 and 20,000 from economic development expenses were approved, and a 2027 calendar with no August meeting was adopted.
decisions: Approved sending a letter that endorses a zoning change for downtown housing and asks for faster review and scheduling of a public hearing.
Approved moving 30,000 from economic development expenses to the facade improvement grant program account.
Approved moving 20,000 from economic development expenses to the small business grant program account.
Approved the 2027 meeting calendar, which has no August meeting.
discussion: Downtown zoning change: A timeline given put approval in March or April. The letter asks staff to speed up the review and scheduling of the public hearing.

Sessions project progress: JHM Group presented work on 273 and 296 Riverside Avenue, including historic review, environmental checks, and design. A draft purchase and sale agreement will come to the board later.
Chippany golf course: The city took ownership and has an RFP out for management. The restaurant operator is set to change to a moderately priced menu within the next week.
Vaping moratorium: The moratorium has not been scheduled for a public hearing or voted on yet. A request to rent space for a vape and smoke shop showed that no protection is in place.

Forestville factory master plan: A proposed master plan for large multi-tenant buildings, such as 61 East Main Street, would let staff review new tenants without a new special permit and site plan each time.
